shared_elements: T-shaped monolithic stone pillar with broad horizontal head over a narrower shaft
low-relief quadruped animal in profile on the shaft
relief confined to the upper part of the shaft, just below the head
excavation setting with dry-stone rubble walling behind
justification:
Both are the same species of object 
dash  a T-headed stone pillar whose shaft carries shallow, flat-topped relief carving of a profile quadruped set immediately beneath the projecting head 
dash  and the carving technique (low, smoothly rounded relief cut back from a flat ground) looks comparable. The decisive difference is density and complexity: A is crowded with multiple registers (a row of animals along the head, a horizontal zigzag/net band, several beasts, a small anthropomorphic figure, birds and a snake-like form), whereas B bears essentially one isolated animal on an otherwise blank shaft.
